Potential mechanism of OA ameliorating central cognitive impairment

Schematic diagram of potential mechanism of OA ameliorating central cognitive impairment. OA interacts with PKC and PI3Kγ to activate downstream signaling cascades of mAChRs, thereby promoting ACh synthesis and release to potentiate hippocampal cholinergic neurotransmission. Additionally, OA activates MEK, which propagates signaling through the ERK/CREB/BDNF axis; this cascade enhances synaptic plasticity, as well as memory formation and consolidation. Furthermore, OA modulates IP3R to maintain intracellular Ca2+ homeostasis, alleviating ROS-induced neuronal damage and mitigating the oxidative stress state in the hippocampus. Collectively, OA may exert a multi-pathway regulatory effect to attenuate core pathological processes linked to cognitive impairment, thereby effectively ameliorating SCOP-induced central cognitive impairment. Red arrows in the diagram indicate the potential molecular targets of OA. (For interpretation of the references to colour in this figure legend, the reader is referred to the web version of this article.)
